limitations: Nine metric passes are descriptive execution results, not new independently adjudicated legitimate Official Pass@1 or a representative benchmark success estimate.
Each program has only three successful scored repetitions out of five attempts. No program has five evaluable agreements; do not claim stability was proven.
Absence of a semantic disagreement in this selected, partially censored sample does not refute the historical python-control observation.
Explicit timeout evidence supports an external-delivery contribution, not necessarily exclusive attribution of every downstream resolver failure.
Two-second read-only filesystem samples are not a complete final environment inventory. Equal dist-info directory names do not establish equal package bytes or all environment state.
Historical final dependency inventories and generated files were not retained, so the historical semantic failure root cause remains unresolved.

recommendation.main_contradiction: Terminal outcomes vary largely before effective scoring; no new strong-Agent semantic repair opportunity was established.
recommendation.support: Identical full programs can terminate differently under the same recorded image and executor; target execution matters operationally.
recommendation.counterevidence: Every scored completion passes and its full diagnostics agree within program; no Agent or feedback treatment was tested.
